ai_analysis.summary: Strong technical fit: the candidate's Linux kernel driver project (SPI, character device) and STM32/UART/I2C embedded work map almost directly onto the job's core requirements, and C/C++ + GDB/valgrind proficiency is well documented. The biggest gap is lack of direct product-firmware or drone/accessory experience and limited real-world industrial embedded deployment beyond academic projects; overall fit is around 75%.
resume_tips: Move the RFID Linux kernel driver project to the top — it directly matches the 'Linux kernel modules' requirement.
Explicitly mention 'firmware' and 'embedded accessory/product' vocabulary since the job targets drone controller firmware, not generic systems work.
Add LTTng or tracing-tool experience if any — the job explicitly cites gdb/valgrind/ltt as debug stack; currently only strace/gdb/valgrind appear.
Quantify RAM/FLASH/CPU-constraint work in the STM32 and RFID driver projects to mirror the job's emphasis on resource-constrained embedded design.
De-emphasize freelance full-stack/web experience — irrelevant to this embedded firmware role and dilutes focus.
Highlight basic electronics skills (I2C/UART wiring, schematic reading) more prominently since the job appreciates them.
ai_analysis.recommended_profile: Looking for a full-time position in software engineering with a focus on embedded Linux firmware development in C/C++. MSc in Computer Engineering (EPITA - GISTRE) in Systems / Embedded. Fluent in French and English (TOEIC 915, C1). Interests: watchmaking, music, hiking/running, cooking.
